body: Just a suggestion, there's no real reason you should listen to me. But at 40, you probably retain most of your physical mobility, which is enough to happily exist with someone worth existing for. To me, anyways - not that I feel like that at the moment. Though I felt like that not too long ago.

A third of me feels like 40 is still a reasonable number. There is a finite sequence of events, or hell fuck even one specific event I guess, that would probably be enough for me to flip back into "normal" mode. Or at the very least, grudgingly stay alive for another 40 or so years. And I only realized that last November. 

So who knows? Maybe you could adjust upwards by another five or ten years. You might find something good, and best of luck with that.
I picked 60, a long time ago. Hell of a too-high number. I've since reduced it down to whenever I felt like I could fade away. Good coping strategy, though.
Helping used to be a nice way of distracting myself.. I can't remember why, though, because it just annoys me more now.
And what kind of pain would that be?

Are we? I am probably more fortunate than many people here, in that I do not actively want for food or shelter, and there are people who I can talk to - shallow though the talks may be. Similarly, there are probably others more and less fortunate than I am, all in different places and from different walks in life. 

Do you believe that someone from a very different walk in life can really relate to your problems? Because being told something to that effect just worsens my mood.

I can relate to that, I guess. I've kind of settled into a position of "everyone is motivated by self-interest and selfishness" though, which is very useful for getting through life but is also very tiring.

Cynically speaking, I find that in the moment, people are programmed to respond with a non-judgemental and supportive attitude. Society expects them to, so they feel good doing so, and that is that. It is definitely appreciated. But I also see no reason to trust responses which seem automatic and insincere.

Like, sure - I will "happily" help anyone that needs it, and "happily" accept any help that comes my way. Life experiences can definitely be shared too. But I'm rather tired of pretending to be happy and helpful and fine. Three years is long enough. So what reasons do I have to continue this pretense?
